wu: Christmas Memory Chain: Students stand in a circle. Student 1 says 'I decorated a Christmas tree.' Student 2 says 'Student 1 decorated a Christmas tree and I wrapped a present.' Continue, with each student repeating the previous chain and adding a new sentence using a past regular verb.
wuAlt: Christmas Vocabulary Race: Write past regular verbs on the board in a list. Students race to write a Christmas-related sentence for each verb.
Find Someone Who...: Students walk around asking 'Did you...?' questions about Christmas activities, e.g., 'Did you bake cookies?' and write names.
pres: Show a 3-panel comic strip of a Christmas story. Model the story in direct speech: 'He said, "I wrapped the gift."' Then rewrite it as reported speech: 'He said (that) he had wrapped the gift.' Highlight the 'said (that)' structure and the verb change. Check understanding by asking students to point to the 'said' and the past verb in a new example.
presAlt: Use a short audio clip of two friends talking about Christmas. Transcribe the direct speech on the board, then transform it into reported speech.
Show a video clip of a Christmas scene. Pause and elicit direct speech sentences, then rewrite them as reported speech on the board.
prac: Reported Speech Relay: In teams, students take turns rewriting a direct speech sentence (on a card) into reported speech on the board. Each student can only write one word. The first team to finish correctly wins. Support by providing a sentence frame: 'He/She said (that)...'
pracAlt: Matching Pairs: Prepare cards with direct speech sentences and their reported speech equivalents. Students match them in pairs.
Correct the Reporter: Give students a worksheet with incorrect reported speech sentences. They work in pairs to find and fix the mistakes.
ls: Listen to a 2-minute podcast where three teens discuss their Christmas traditions. Students listen and fill in a table with the names of the speakers and their traditions in reported speech, e.g., 'Amina said (that) she visited her grandparents.'
re: Verb Charades: After the break, act out a past regular verb related to Christmas (e.g., 'wrapping', 'singing'). Students shout the verb in the past form. The first to guess correctly becomes the next actor.
prod: Christmas Panel Discussion: In groups of three, students roleplay a panel discussing 'What Christmas means to us.' Each student takes a turn to make a statement about their experience (direct speech), and the others must report it back to the group. Encourage 2-minute turns per student.
rw: Read a short news article about how teens in different countries celebrate Christmas. Students underline all the reported verbs (e.g., 'explained', 'mentioned') and write three of their own reported sentences about the text, e.g., 'The article said (that) teens in Japan eat fried chicken.'
st: Read 'The Gift of the Magi' by O. Henry (abridged version). Discuss the ending, then close with the goodbye routine: 'Today we practiced retelling stories in reported speech. Thank you for your hard work and have a great day!'
g: Create bingo cards with reported speech sentences. Call out direct speech sentences; students mark the matching reported speech.
Groups write a story one sentence at a time, using past regular verbs and reported speech.
Students crumble paper with past regular verbs and toss them. When a verb lands, they must use it in a reported speech sentence.
Read a mix of direct and reported speech sentences. Students stand up if it's reported speech.
Draw a Christmas activity; others guess and then report it: 'He/She drew (that) he was decorating a tree.'
diff: Fast finishers: Write a short paragraph (60 words) retelling their own Christmas memory using reported speech.
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence frame with a word bank to complete reported sentences: 'He said (that) he _______ (verb) a _______ (noun).'
hw: Read the Christmas article again and write three more reported sentences about it.
Write a 60-word email to a friend describing your Christmas using at least five past regular verbs.
Record a 1-minute audio retelling a Christmas story using reported speech.
tip: Emphasize the connection between reported speech and storytelling, as it's a key skill for the PET speaking exam. For Moroccan students, relate the theme to universal values of family and giving, avoiding religious specifics to respect cultural diversity.
